clue.text: Piano score on record by one showing self-control

indicators.note: on here means placed after, so the piano and score pieces follow the record and one

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
I is the Roman numeral for one
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
to score is to mark a line, so score gives line

explanation.surface: A pianist with a recorded score shows great self-control.
explanation.definitionFit: Discipline is the habit of controlling one's own behaviour, a direct synonym of self-control.

clue.text: Listened to songs in lounge

indicators.note: something listened to is heard rather than read, so the word for songs is taken by its sound

parts.note: lays are old songs or ballads

explanation.surface: Someone listened to songs while relaxing in a lounge.
explanation.definitionFit: To lounge is to idle or loaf about, which is what laze means as a verb.

clue.text: Unpleasant chap has pastry case with middle bit removed

parts.note: a chap is a male

indicators.note: a middle chunk of the pastry word is cut out, leaving its two ends

parts.note: a vol-au-vent is a small puff-pastry case

explanation.surface: An unpleasant man has eaten the centre out of his vol-au-vent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with middle bit removed' takes AUV from the middle of VOLAUVENT, leaving VOLENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Malevolent means wishing harm to others, a strong form of unpleasant.

clue.text: In Provence I will reserve a few weeks in early summer

indicators.note: to reserve is to hold something, so the French I holds the French a

parts.note: in French, spoken in Provence, I is je
the French indefinite article un, continuing the French setting

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker in Provence plans to book a few weeks at the start of summer.
explanation.walkthrough: The French setting from 'In Provence' carries over to 'a', which is read as the French article; 'will reserve' means holds inside.
explanation.definitionFit: June is the month at the start of summer, about four weeks long.

clue.text: When the sun is up proper, outlaw gets much put about

indicators.note: the outlaw and much pieces are placed around the word for proper

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
right means proper or correct
dearly means very much, as in loved dearly

explanation.surface: A gangster spreads word when the sun rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proper' and 'outlaw' look like adjective and noun together, but they are separate pieces; 'put about' means placed around.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright and early is an idiom for first thing in the morning, just after sunrise.

clue.text: On craft perhaps overseas, right to go some way east

indicators.note: in an across clue east is rightwards, so the R travels a couple of places towards the end

parts.note: abroad means overseas

explanation.surface: Overseas, someone's rights extend a little further east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go some way east' shifts the R in ABROAD two places along, giving A-B-O-A-R-D.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboard means on a ship or aircraft; 'perhaps' marks a craft as only one example.

clue.text: Way to pay cost of parking at hospital

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay the cost
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A complaint about having to pay for parking at a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A footpath is a way or track for walkers.

clue.text: Limit unspecified number entering French O-level

indicators.note: the number goes into the run of French, O and level

parts.note: the letter O plus level, which gives tier, a layer or level
n is the mathematical symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: A school cap on how many can take the French O-level exam.
explanation.walkthrough: O-level was the old British exam taken at about 16; here it splits into O and TIER. 'entering' puts N into FROTIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontier is a border, the limit of a territory or field of knowledge.

clue.text: Signal how to dupe people?

definitions.meaning: a light or fire used as a warning sign
read as three words it says ..., the way to trick people

explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a fire or light lit as a signal or warning.

clue.text: Playing in hotel, brother accompanying old American jazz musician

indicators.note: playing suggests letters performing in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a monk is a brother in a religious order

explanation.surface: An old American jazz musician plays in a hotel alongside his brother.
explanation.definitionFit: Thelonious Monk was the American bebop pianist and composer, a celebrated jazz musician.

clue.text: Horse — farm animal — eating a gull

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

indicators.note: the farm animal takes the a inside it

parts.note: an ox is a farm animal

explanation.surface: A horse and an ox on the farm share their feed with a seagull.
explanation.definitionFit: To gull someone is to trick or dupe them, the same as to pull a trick on them.

clue.text: Rabbit races in unusual location

indicators.note: the races are put inside the rearranged letters
unusual means the letters are out of their normal order

parts.note: taken as written
the TT are the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Races are held in an unusual place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges the letters of location; the TT are the Isle of Man motorbike races.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottontail is an American rabbit named for its white fluffy tail.

clue.text: Tricks dimwits out of a penny

indicators.note: the penny is taken out of the word for dimwits

parts.note: dopes are dimwits
p stands for a penny

explanation.surface: Fools are tricked out of a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is slang for to cheat or swindle them, so does means tricks.

clue.text: Daughter showing no warmth about tin proffered by people begging

indicators.note: the daughter piece is offered by the people, who come first

parts.note: men means people

indicators.note: the cold word goes around the tin

parts.note: icy means cold, showing no warmth
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A cold daughter is handed a collecting tin by beggars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proffered by people' puts the people piece first; 'about' means around the tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendicancy is the practice of begging for a living.

clue.text: Stupid cartoon film has ending cut

indicators.note: the last letter of the film title is cut off

parts.note: Dumbo is the Disney cartoon about a flying elephant

explanation.surface: A dull cartoon is shortened at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumb means stupid in informal and especially American use.

clue.text: Sister drinks beer? No, port

indicators.note: the sister takes the beer inside her

parts.note: ale is beer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nun turns down a beer, preferring port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the fortified wine but is an Italian harbour city; 'beer? No' reads as a refusal, but No is a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Salerno is a port city on the south-west coast of Italy.

clue.text: Home before five, I proceed to hand out refreshment

parts.note: in means at home
V is the Roman numeral for five
to go is to proceed
to ration is to hand out in fixed portions

explanation.surface: Someone home before five goes off to serve refreshments.
explanation.definitionFit: Invigoration is being given new energy, a kind of refreshment.

clue.text: Learner with old books overlooks a work by Russian-American

indicators.note: in a down clue to overlook is to sit above, so the books come before the a

parts.note: L is the learner plate
lit is short for literature, books

explanation.surface: A student with old books ignores one Russian-American author's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooks' looks like 'ignores' but in a down entry means 'sits above'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolita is the 1955 novel by Vladimir Nabokov, a Russian-born American writer.

clue.text: Religious lady, one in twelve shunning group of workers?

indicators.note: the nun and the one go inside the twelve

parts.note: noon is twelve o'clock
a nun is a religious woman
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A nun, one of twelve, stays clear of a workers' group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in twelve' suggests a fraction or a disciple; twelve is the time of day here.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-union workplace or worker is one that does not belong to a trade union.

clue.text: With a couple of pints almost tops up water tanks

indicators.note: the last letter of the quart word is left off

parts.note: a quart is two pints

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the piece is read from the bottom

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, tops

explanation.surface: Someone tops up water tanks with nearly two pints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops T from QUART; 'up' turns AI into IA. A1 is written AI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquaria is a plural of aquarium, a tank for keeping fish in water.

clue.text: All skin and bone on the inside, say?

indicators.note: the very thin phrase goes inside the abbreviation for say

parts.note: eg, for example, is signalled by say
someone all skin and bone is very thin

explanation.surface: Someone is all skin and bone inside, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All skin and bone' reads as one phrase, but 'All' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Everything means all things, the whole lot.

clue.text: You and I start to celebrate after mastering foreign languages

indicators.note: the start of celebrate comes after the rearranged mastering

parts.note: you and I together are we

indicators.note: foreign suggests letters moved out of their familiar order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first letter of celebrate

explanation.surface: We start celebrating after learning foreign languages.
explanation.definitionFit: West Germanic is the branch of languages including English, German and Dutch.

clue.text: Imported from Asia? Unlikely

definitions.meaning: brought in from a distant place, literally fetched from far off

explanation.definitionFit: Far-fetched means improbable or hard to believe, so unlikely.

clue.text: National uprising, I note

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: The Times is a national newspaper
I as the Roman numeral is one

explanation.surface: A nationwide revolt, I would observe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns TIMES into SEMIT; 'National' suggests a country but is the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A semitone is the interval between adjacent notes, loosely used for a half-step note.

clue.text: Work out initially what gym costs?

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of out

parts.note: PE is physical education, school gym
a rate is a charge or cost

explanation.surface: Someone works out what their gym membership costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out' looks like one phrasal verb, but 'Work' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate is to work or function, as a machine does.

clue.text: Curb Tory team, oddly getting elected

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, a Tory

indicators.note: oddly takes the first and third letters of team

parts.note: in means elected, as a party voted in

explanation.surface: A Conservative team gets elected and restrains itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To contain something is to curb or hold it back.

clue.text: Pursued old German fellow in drainpipes?

parts.note: the Huns were an ancient people; Hun is an old slang term for a German
a Ted, or Teddy boy, wore narrow drainpipe trousers

explanation.surface: An old German man was chased through the drainpipes.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style clothes and tight drainpipe trousers; drainpipes here are trousers, not plumbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunted means chased or pursued.

clue.text: Building material used in erection of royal castle

indicators.note: erection of says the hidden letters are read backwards
used in says the letters sit inside the words royal castle

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A building material used to put up a royal castle.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took 'used', leaving the hiding with no indicator; 'used in' signals the hidden run, and 'erection of' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Clay is used for bricks and tiles, a basic building material.
